1:1.t: Micah came from Moresheth, a village in the foothills of Judah, and prophesied from about 740 to 700 BC, at the same time as Isaiah.

1:10.t: Each town's name is a wordplay: Gath sounds like "tell"; Beth Ophrah ("house of dust"), roll in the dust; Shaphir ("beautiful") will go in shame; Zaanan ("come out") will not come out; Maroth ("bitter"); Lachish sounds like "team of horses"; Akzib ("deception") will deceive; Mareshah sounds like "conqueror". "Tell it not in Gath" echoes 2 Samuel 1:20.

2:7.t: "Does the LORD become impatient?": the KJV's "is the spirit of the LORD straitened?"

2:12.t: "In a pen": the KJV's "as the sheep of Bozrah".

3:12.t: This prophecy was remembered a century later, when it saved Jeremiah's life (Jeremiah 26:18-19).

4:1.t: Isaiah 2:2-4 contains nearly the same prophecy.

4:8.t: "Watchtower of the flock": the KJV's "tower of the flock", Hebrew migdal eder.

5:1.t: In the Hebrew text this verse is 4:14, and 5:1-15 is 5:1-14 with the numbering shifted by one.

5:2.t: "Clans": the KJV's "thousands", the units into which a tribe was divided.

"Bethlehem Ephrathah ... out of you will come for Me One who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old": David's town will produce a greater King, whose origins reach back to eternity. When the wise men asked where the Messiah would be born, the chief priests quoted this verse (Matthew 2:5-6). Following this reading, His pronouns are capitalized in verses 2-5.

5:6.t: Nimrod: the founder of Assyria's cities (Genesis 10:8-12).

6:5.t: Balaam blessed Israel instead of cursing it (Numbers 22-24). From Shittim, the last camp east of the Jordan, Israel crossed to Gilgal (Joshua 3-4).

6:9.t: "To fear Your name is wisdom": the KJV's "the man of wisdom shall see thy name".

6:16.t: Omri and Ahab: kings of Israel known for idolatry (1 Kings 16).

7:4.t: "The day God visits you": the KJV's "thy visitation", the day of judgment.

7:12.t: "Egypt ... the Euphrates": the KJV's "the fortified cities ... the river"; the Hebrew matsor can mean either "fortress" or "Egypt".

2:13.t: "The One who breaks open the way" (Hebrew happorets): the KJV's "The breaker". God goes ahead of His people like a shepherd breaking through the wall of the pen, leading them out to freedom.

4:4.t: "Everyone will sit under their own vine and under their own fig tree": a proverbial picture of peace and security (1 Kings 4:25, Zechariah 3:10).

5:5.t: "He will be our peace" (Hebrew vehayah zeh shalom): see Isaiah 9:6 and Ephesians 2:14, "He Himself is our peace".

6:8.t: "To act justly and to love steadfast love and to walk humbly with your God" (Hebrew asot mishpat ve'ahavat chesed vehatsnea lekhet im eloheikha): the KJV's "to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God". God wants not more sacrifices but justice toward others, a heart that loves hesed, and humble fellowship with Him.

7:6.t: Jesus quotes this verse in Matthew 10:35-36.

7:18.t: "Who is a God like You?": a wordplay on Micah's name, which means "Who is like the LORD?" God "delights to show steadfast love" (chafets chesed) and hurls sins into the depths of the sea, gone forever.
